why: A script `app/probe.m` first on the path, a function `lib/probe.m` farther. MATLAB R2026a (the lead's run): a statement and `probe()` run the script, `h()` on a handle to it runs it, `probe(2)` and `h(2)` error. So `probe( )` (empty, a space), a statement `probe` in an `if` line, `feval(@probe)`, `run('probe')` and `f = str2func('probe'); f()` run the script; `feval(@probe, 1)`, `f(1)` and `cellfun(@probe, {1})` (which calls `probe(1)`) error and call no `lib/probe.m`. And `v = probe();`, which asks the script for an output, errors as `v = probe;` does (R2026a; a script returns nothing, doc 'Scripts vs Functions'): a live row, no call (the empty argument list runs a script only as a statement of its own).
